speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear about your chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been occurring and if they have been worsening over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history. Given the pain relief after voiding and recent dyspareunia, I need to know if you have experienced any fever, chills, visible blood in your urine, or flank pain recently?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.
REQUEST TEST: Urine_cytology.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None. Urine Cytology: Not performed in current dataset.

speaker: Patient
text: ul intercourse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand the previous doctor suspected a urinary tract infection, but your symptoms of significant pain relief after voiding and dyspareunia are more characteristic of an inflammatory condition like interstitial cystitis or urethral syndrome. Did you have any difficulty starting your urine stream, a weak stream, or any sensation of incomplete emptying?

REQUEST TEST: Post-void residual volume.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Postvoid Residual Urine: 25 mL. Pelvic Ultrasound: Normal postvoid residual urine volume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal ultrasound and low post-void residual, have you noticed any pelvic pressure or a specific trigger for your pain, such as caffeine, acidic foods, or stress? Also, has your doctor ever ordered a cystoscopy to rule out Hunner's lesions or other structural abnormalities? REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cystoscopy: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis / Painful Bladder Syndrome
